# Overview

**Question.** With the same nine hitters, does a Traditional batting order (A) or an OPS-ranked order (B) produce more expected runs? Five teams (Dodgers, Cubs, Cardinals, Angels, Giants), 2023-2026 regular seasons, 20 team-seasons.

**Key results.** The two orders give practically the same expected runs in all 20 team-seasons. In 2 team-seasons the rules produce the identical lineup. In the other 18, B minus A ranges from −0.006 to +0.020 runs per game, or −1 to +3 runs over 162 games. Across team-seasons the mean difference is 0.0015 runs per game (95% CI −0.0014 to 0.0045, *p* = 0.30). Reversing a lineup costs 0.06-0.19 runs per game, so the model does respond to order; A and B are simply too similar. The result holds under the PM notebook's choices (same-season statistics, fixed base-running rules).

**Pipeline.** This file runs every step, in order:

1. **Data collection.** Play-by-play for every regular-season game of the five teams, official player and team statistics, all from the MLB Stats API.
2. **Cleaning and checks.** Each team-season's play-by-play counts must match its official totals.
3. **Two clean tables** replace the supplied workbooks: player statistics and player outcome probabilities for 2023-2026 (`clean/`). A section compares them with the supplied files.
4. **Hitters and orders.** Each team-season's nine regulars. Orders A and B follow the scope's rules, using each hitter's **previous-season** OBP, SLG, and OPS, which is what a manager knows before the season.
5. **Simulation model.** Each hitter's outcome rates for that season and base-out transitions estimated from that season's play-by-play. A Markov chain gives exact expected runs; a Monte Carlo simulation checks it.
6. **Results, model checks, and stability checks.**

To reproduce, Knit in RStudio or run `rmarkdown::render("MLB_Lineup_Simulation.Rmd")`. If `source_cache/` from an earlier run is in the same folder, the Knit runs offline in about 5 minutes. Otherwise the first run downloads about 3,000 game files into `source_cache/`, which needs network access and takes over an hour. The comparison with the supplied workbooks runs only when the two `.xlsx` files are in the same folder.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE)
for (d in c("source_cache/api/games", "clean", "processed", "quality")) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
seasons <- 2023:2026
team_ids <- c(Dodgers = 119, Cubs = 112, Cardinals = 138, Angels = 108, Giants = 137)
api <- "https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1"
supplied_files <- c(stats = "Math 534 Baseball Project-2.xlsx", probs = "MLB_2023_2026_5Teams_Player_Probabilities.xlsx")
have_supplied <- all(file.exists(supplied_files))  # the workbook comparison is skipped without them
```

# Data Collection

## API Helpers

Every response is saved under `source_cache/` on first use, so later Knits are offline and give the same answer.

```{r api-functions}
get_json <- function(url, file) {
  if (!file.exists(file)) {
    download.file(url, paste0(file, ".part"), quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    file.rename(paste0(file, ".part"), file)
  }
  jsonlite::fromJSON(file, simplifyVector = FALSE)
}
val <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) NA else x  # missing JSON field becomes NA
stat_row <- function(s) data.frame(
  g = val(s$gamesPlayed), pa = s$plateAppearances, ab = s$atBats, r = val(s$runs), h = s$hits, d2 = s$doubles,
  d3 = s$triples, hr = s$homeRuns, rbi = val(s$rbi), bb = s$baseOnBalls, ibb = val(s$intentionalWalks),
  hbp = s$hitByPitch, so = s$strikeOuts, sf = s$sacFlies, sb = val(s$stolenBases), cs = val(s$caughtStealing))

# Season hitting totals for every MLB player (a traded player has one row, all teams combined).
league_hitting <- function(season) {
  url <- paste0(api, "/stats?stats=season&group=hitting&gameType=R&playerPool=ALL&sportIds=1&limit=10000&season=", season)
  bind_rows(lapply(get_json(url, sprintf("source_cache/api/league_%d.json", season))$stats[[1]]$splits, function(p)
    data.frame(season = season, batter_id = as.character(p$player$id), player = p$player$fullName, stat_row(p$stat))))
}

# Season hitting totals for a whole team.
team_hitting <- function(season, team) {
  url <- paste0(api, "/teams/", team_ids[[team]], "/stats?stats=season&group=hitting&gameType=R&season=", season)
  s <- get_json(url, sprintf("source_cache/api/teamtotal_%d_%s.json", season, team))$stats[[1]]$splits[[1]]$stat
  data.frame(season = season, team = team, stat_row(s))
}

# Regular-season games that were played to a final result.
final_games <- function(season, team) {
  url <- paste0(api, "/schedule?sportId=1&gameType=R&season=", season, "&teamId=", team_ids[[team]],
                "&fields=dates,date,games,gamePk,status,abstractGameState,detailedState,teams,away,home,team,id,score")
  d <- get_json(url, sprintf("source_cache/api/sched_%d_%s.json", season, team))
  unlist(lapply(d$dates, function(dt) unlist(lapply(dt$games, function(g)
    if (g$status$abstractGameState == "Final" && !grepl("Postponed|Cancelled|Suspended", g$status$detailedState))
      as.character(g$gamePk)))))
}

# Player records with year-by-year hitting lines, in batches of 100 IDs.
get_people <- function(ids) {
  batches <- split(ids, ceiling(seq_along(ids) / 100))
  unlist(lapply(batches, function(b) {
    url <- paste0(api, "/people?personIds=", paste(b, collapse = ","), "&hydrate=stats(group=[hitting],type=[yearByYear])")
    file <- sprintf("source_cache/api/people_%s_%d.json", b[1], length(b))
    z <- get_json(url, file)$people
    if (!setequal(vapply(z, function(p) as.character(p$id), ""), b)) {  # cached file is for another ID set
      unlink(file)
      z <- get_json(url, file)$people
    }
    z
  }), recursive = FALSE)
}
# Each player's official season line for each of the five teams he played for.
team_splits <- function(people) {
  bind_rows(lapply(people, function(p) {
    splits <- unlist(lapply(p$stats, `[[`, "splits"), recursive = FALSE)
    bind_rows(lapply(splits, function(s) {
      tid <- val(s$team$id)
      if (is.na(tid) || !tid %in% team_ids || !as.integer(s$season) %in% seasons) return(NULL)
      data.frame(season = as.integer(s$season), team = names(team_ids)[match(tid, team_ids)],
                 batter_id = as.character(p$id), player = p$fullName, stat_row(s$stat))
    }))
  }))
}
```

## Play-by-Play, 2023-2026

Every regular-season game involving the five teams, both offenses. For each play: the inning, the event, the outs and runners after the play, and the batting team's score. Each season's parsed plays are also cached, so a re-Knit does not parse 3,000 files again.

```{r game-feeds}
game_fields <- paste(c("gameData", "status", "abstractGameState", "teams", "away", "home", "id", "liveData", "plays",
                       "allPlays", "about", "inning", "halfInning", "result", "eventType", "awayScore", "homeScore",
                       "count", "outs", "matchup", "batter", "postOnFirst", "postOnSecond", "postOnThird"), collapse = ",")
read_plays <- function(g) {
  z <- get_json(paste0("https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1.1/game/", g, "/feed/live?fields=", game_fields),
                sprintf("source_cache/api/games/%s.json", g))
  ap <- z$liveData$plays$allPlays
  half <- vapply(ap, function(p) p$about$halfInning, "")
  data.frame(game_id = g, state = z$gameData$status$abstractGameState, play = seq_along(ap),
             batting_team_id = ifelse(half == "top", z$gameData$teams$away$id, z$gameData$teams$home$id),
             inning = vapply(ap, function(p) as.integer(p$about$inning), 1L), half = half,
             batter_id = vapply(ap, function(p) as.character(p$matchup$batter$id), ""),
             event = vapply(ap, function(p) as.character(val(p$result$eventType)), ""),
             outs = vapply(ap, function(p) as.integer(val(p$count$outs)), 1L),
             score = vapply(seq_along(ap), function(i)
               as.numeric(val(ap[[i]]$result[[paste0(if (half[i] == "top") "away" else "home", "Score")]])), 1),
             on1 = vapply(ap, function(p) !is.null(p$matchup$postOnFirst), TRUE),
             on2 = vapply(ap, function(p) !is.null(p$matchup$postOnSecond), TRUE),
             on3 = vapply(ap, function(p) !is.null(p$matchup$postOnThird), TRUE))
}
season_plays <- function(season) {
  ids <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(names(team_ids), function(t) final_games(season, t)))))
  file <- sprintf("source_cache/plays_%d.rds", season)
  if (file.exists(file)) {
    d <- readRDS(file)
    if (setequal(unique(d$game_id), ids)) return(d)
  }
  d <- bind_rows(lapply(ids, read_plays)) %>% mutate(season = season)
  saveRDS(d, file)
  d
}
raw_plays <- bind_rows(lapply(seasons, season_plays))
raw_plays %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(games = n_distinct(game_id), plays = n())
```

## Official Statistics

```{r official-stats}
league <- bind_rows(lapply(2021:2026, league_hitting))  # 2021-2022 are needed for the 2023 orders
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(league[c("season", "batter_id")]))
team_totals <- bind_rows(lapply(seasons, function(y) bind_rows(lapply(names(team_ids), function(t) team_hitting(y, t)))))
table(season = league$season)
```

# Cleaning and Checks

## Plate-Appearance Outcomes

Eight outcomes. BB includes intentional walks and hit-by-pitch. ROE is reached on error or catcher's interference. OUT is every other plate appearance: outs in play, double plays, sacrifices, fielder's choice.

```{r plays}
categories <- c("1B", "2B", "3B", "HR", "BB", "ROE", "K", "OUT")
event_category <- c(
  single = "1B", double = "2B", triple = "3B", home_run = "HR",
  walk = "BB", intent_walk = "BB", hit_by_pitch = "BB", field_error = "ROE", catcher_interf = "ROE",
  strikeout = "K", strikeout_double_play = "K", strikeout_triple_play = "K",
  field_out = "OUT", force_out = "OUT", grounded_into_double_play = "OUT", grounded_into_triple_play = "OUT",
  double_play = "OUT", triple_play = "OUT", sac_fly = "OUT", sac_fly_double_play = "OUT", sac_bunt = "OUT",
  sac_bunt_double_play = "OUT", fielders_choice = "OUT", fielders_choice_out = "OUT", batter_interference = "OUT")
# Plays that end without a completed plate appearance; they change the state but are not outcomes.
non_pa_events <- c("caught_stealing_2b", "caught_stealing_3b", "caught_stealing_home", "pickoff_1b", "pickoff_2b",
                   "pickoff_3b", "pickoff_caught_stealing_2b", "pickoff_caught_stealing_3b",
                   "pickoff_caught_stealing_home", "pickoff_error_1b", "pickoff_error_2b", "pickoff_error_3b",
                   "stolen_base_2b", "stolen_base_3b", "stolen_base_home", "wild_pitch", "passed_ball", "balk",
                   "other_advance", "other_out", "runner_double_play", "error", "defensive_indiff")
n_runners <- function(b) b %% 2 + b %/% 2 %% 2 + b %/% 4

plays <- raw_plays %>%
  mutate(category = unname(event_category[event]), is_pa = !is.na(category),
         bases = on1 + 2L * on2 + 4L * on3,
         team = names(team_ids)[match(batting_team_id, team_ids)]) %>%
  group_by(game_id, half) %>% arrange(play, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(runs = score - lag(score, default = 0)) %>%
  group_by(game_id, inning, half) %>%
  mutate(pre_outs = lag(outs, default = 0L), pre_bases = lag(bases, default = 0L),
         runs_rest = rev(cumsum(rev(runs))), last_play = row_number() == n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(used = inning <= 8 | (inning == 9 & half == "top"),
         balanced = outs == 3 |
           n_runners(pre_bases) + is_pa == n_runners(bases) + runs + outs - pre_outs)
table(category = plays$category, useNA = "ifany")
```

`NA` rows are steals, pickoffs, and other plays without a completed plate appearance. `balanced` checks that every runner and the batter is accounted for: runners before plus the batter equal runners after plus runs plus new outs. Only innings 1-8 and the top of the 9th feed the transition model (`used`), because a walk-off can end the bottom of the 9th early and extra innings start with a runner on second.

## Play-by-Play Checks

The key check: for every team-season, the play-by-play counts of each outcome equal the team's official season totals. Official totals do not separate ROE, so ROE and OUT are compared together.

```{r play-checks}
used <- plays %>% filter(used)
official_counts <- function(d) with(d, cbind(`1B` = h - d2 - d3 - hr, `2B` = d2, `3B` = d3, HR = hr, BB = bb + hbp,
                                             K = so, `ROE+OUT` = pa - h - bb - hbp - so))
feed_counts <- plays %>% filter(is_pa, !is.na(team)) %>%
  mutate(category = ifelse(category %in% c("ROE", "OUT"), "ROE+OUT", category)) %>%
  count(season, team, category) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = n) %>%
  arrange(season, team)
team_totals <- team_totals %>% arrange(season, team)
stat_counts <- data.frame(team_totals[c("season", "team")], official_counts(team_totals), check.names = FALSE)
count_cols_check <- colnames(official_counts(team_totals))
unknown_events <- setdiff(unique(plays$event), c(names(event_category), non_pa_events))

play_checks <- plays %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(
  "All games are final" = all(state == "Final"),
  "Every play is classified" = all(event %in% c(names(event_category), non_pa_events)),
  "Outs never decrease within a half-inning" = all(outs >= pre_outs & outs <= 3),
  "No negative runs" = all(runs >= 0),
  "Innings 1-8 end with three outs (99.5%)" = mean(outs[used & last_play & inning <= 8] == 3) > 0.995,
  "Runners balance on 99.5% of used plays" = mean(balanced[used]) > 0.995) %>%
  left_join(bind_rows(lapply(seasons, function(y) data.frame(season = y,
    "Outcome counts match official team totals" =
      all(as.matrix(feed_counts[feed_counts$season == y, count_cols_check]) ==
          as.matrix(stat_counts[stat_counts$season == y, count_cols_check])), check.names = FALSE))), by = "season")
knitr::kable(t(play_checks[-1]) %>% `colnames<-`(play_checks$season), caption = "Checks by season")
if (length(unknown_events)) print(unknown_events)
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(play_checks[-1])))
used %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(plays_unbalanced = sum(!balanced), pa_in_model = sum(is_pa & balanced))
```

# Two Clean Tables

## Table 1: Player Statistics

One row per team, season, and hitter: his official line **for that team**, so a traded player's games for another club are not mixed in. The columns follow the supplied `Math 534 Baseball Project` workbook, with the player ID added. Rates are recomputed from the counts.

```{r table-stats}
count_cols <- c("pa", "ab", "h", "d2", "d3", "hr", "bb", "hbp", "so", "sf")
add_rates <- function(d) mutate(d, obp = (h + bb + hbp) / (ab + bb + hbp + sf),
                                slg = (h + d2 + 2 * d3 + 3 * hr) / ab, ops = obp + slg)
pbp_pa <- plays %>% filter(is_pa, !is.na(team)) %>% count(season, team, batter_id, name = "pbp_pa")
people <- get_people(sort(unique(pbp_pa$batter_id)))
player_names <- data.frame(batter_id = vapply(people, function(p) as.character(p$id), ""),
                           player = vapply(people, function(p) p$fullName, ""))
player_stats <- team_splits(people) %>%
  group_by(season, team, batter_id, player) %>%
  summarise(across(c(g, pa, ab, r, h, d2, d3, hr, rbi, bb, ibb, hbp, so, sf, sb, cs), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(pa > 0) %>% add_rates()

pa_compare <- full_join(player_stats %>% select(season, team, batter_id, pa), pbp_pa, by = c("season", "team", "batter_id")) %>%
  mutate(diff = coalesce(pa, 0L) - coalesce(pbp_pa, 0L))
table1_checks <- c(
  "Every play-by-play batter is a known player" = all(pbp_pa$batter_id %in% player_names$batter_id),
  "Team PA sums equal official team totals" = all(
    (player_stats %>% group_by(season, team) %>% summarise(pa = sum(pa), .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(season, team))$pa ==
      team_totals$pa),
  "Player PA within 3 of play-by-play PA" = all(abs(pa_compare$diff) <= 3))
knitr::kable(data.frame(check = names(table1_checks), passed = table1_checks), row.names = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(table1_checks))
c(player_seasons = nrow(pa_compare), exact_pa_match = sum(pa_compare$diff == 0), max_abs_diff = max(abs(pa_compare$diff)))

# Round half up, as MLB does (.3125 -> .313); undefined rates (no AB) become NA.
rate3 <- function(x) ifelse(is.finite(x), floor(x * 1000 + 0.5 + 1e-9) / 1000, NA)
table1 <- player_stats %>% arrange(season, match(team, names(team_ids)), desc(pa)) %>%
  transmute(Team = team, Season = season, Player = player, G = g, AB = ab, R = r, H = h, `2B` = d2, `3B` = d3,
            HR = hr, RBI = rbi, BB = bb, SO = so, SB = sb, CS = cs, AVG = rate3(h / ab), OBP = rate3(obp),
            SLG = rate3(slg), OPS = rate3(ops), PA = pa, `SO/PA` = round(so / pa, 4),
            batter_id = batter_id, HBP = hbp, SF = sf, IBB = ibb)
write.csv(table1, "clean/player_stats_2023_2026.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
table1 %>% count(Season, Team) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Team, values_from = n)
```

The play-by-play can differ from the official line by a plate appearance or two: when a substitute finishes a two-strike count, the strikeout can be charged to the original batter.

## Table 2: Player Outcome Probabilities

One row per team, season, and hitter, from his plate appearances for that team. Columns follow the supplied probabilities workbook. The seven outcome columns sum to 1. `Out` includes strikeouts, and `Strikeout` repeats the strikeout share (part of `Out`).

```{r table-probabilities}
pbp_counts <- plays %>% filter(is_pa, !is.na(team)) %>% count(season, team, batter_id, category) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = category, values_from = n, values_fill = 0L)
for (k in setdiff(categories, names(pbp_counts))) pbp_counts[[k]] <- 0L
pbp_counts <- pbp_counts %>% mutate(pa = rowSums(across(all_of(categories)))) %>%
  left_join(player_names, by = "batter_id")
stopifnot(!anyNA(pbp_counts$player))

table2 <- pbp_counts %>% arrange(season, match(team, names(team_ids)), desc(pa)) %>%
  transmute(team, season, batter_id, player, Single = `1B` / pa, Double = `2B` / pa, Triple = `3B` / pa,
            `Home Run` = HR / pa, `Walk/HBP` = BB / pa, `Error/Interference` = ROE / pa, Out = (K + OUT) / pa,
            PA = pa, Strikeout = K / pa)
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(table2[c("Single", "Double", "Triple", "Home Run", "Walk/HBP", "Error/Interference", "Out")]) - 1) < 1e-9))
write.csv(table2, "clean/player_probabilities_2023_2026.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
table2 %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(
  across(c(Single, Double, Triple, `Home Run`, `Walk/HBP`, `Error/Interference`, Out), ~ round(weighted.mean(.x, PA), 3)),
  hitters = n(), PA = sum(PA))
```

## Comparison with the Supplied Workbooks

Each row of the supplied statistics workbook is matched to Table 1 by team, season, and name (accents removed). A row "matches" when its OBP and SLG agree with the official line to the third decimal.

```{r supplied-stats, eval=have_supplied}
norm_name <- function(x) tolower(trimws(stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "Latin-ASCII")))
near <- function(a, b) !is.na(a) & !is.na(b) & abs(a - b) < 0.0015
supplied_stats <- readxl::read_excel(supplied_files[["stats"]]) %>%
  mutate(Team = recode(Team, Angles = "Angels"), key = norm_name(Player), row = row_number())
# Two players can share a name (there are two Will Smiths); keep the one with more PA.
official <- player_stats %>% arrange(desc(pa)) %>% transmute(team, season, key = norm_name(player), obp, slg, team_pa = pa) %>%
  distinct(team, season, key, .keep_all = TRUE)
season_total <- league %>% add_rates() %>% arrange(desc(pa)) %>%
  transmute(season, key = norm_name(player), obp_all = obp, slg_all = slg) %>% distinct(season, key, .keep_all = TRUE)
stats_check <- supplied_stats %>%
  left_join(official, by = c(Team = "team", Season = "season", key = "key")) %>%
  left_join(official %>% transmute(team, season = season + 1L, key, obp_prev = obp, slg_prev = slg),
            by = c(Team = "team", Season = "season", key = "key")) %>%
  left_join(season_total, by = c(Season = "season", key = "key")) %>%
  group_by(Team, Season, key) %>% mutate(duplicate_name = n() > 1) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(status = case_when(
    near(OBP, obp) & near(SLG, slg) ~ "matches team line",
    near(OBP, obp_all) & near(SLG, slg_all) ~ "matches season total (all teams)",
    near(OBP, obp_prev) & near(SLG, slg_prev) ~ "previous season's line",
    is.na(obp) ~ "not found for this team-season",
    TRUE ~ "does not match"))
knitr::kable(stats_check %>% count(Season, Team, status) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
               left_join(official %>% filter(team_pa >= 150) %>% count(Season = season, Team = team, name = "official hitters with 150+ PA"),
                         by = c("Season", "Team")) %>% arrange(Season, match(Team, names(team_ids))),
             caption = "Supplied statistics workbook, rows by status")
knitr::kable(stats_check %>% filter(status != "matches team line") %>%
               select(Team, Season, Player, PA, OBP, SLG, status, duplicate_name, official_obp = obp, official_slg = slg),
             digits = 3, caption = "Supplied rows that do not match the official team line")
```

The supplied probabilities workbook has player IDs, so its rows are matched to Table 2 by team, season, and ID.

```{r supplied-probs, eval=have_supplied}
prob_cols <- c("Single", "Double", "Triple", "Home Run", "Walk/HBP", "Error/Interference", "Out")
supplied_probs <- readxl::read_excel(supplied_files[["probs"]]) %>%
  mutate(batter_id = as.character(batter_id))
probs_check <- supplied_probs %>%
  inner_join(table2 %>% select(team, season, batter_id, all_of(prob_cols), PA),
             by = c("team", "season", "batter_id"), suffix = c("", "_clean"))
probs_check$rate_diff <- apply(abs(as.matrix(probs_check[prob_cols]) -
                                     as.matrix(probs_check[paste0(prob_cols, "_clean")])), 1, max)
knitr::kable(supplied_probs %>% group_by(season) %>%
               summarise(rows = n(), rows_50_pa = sum(PA >= 50), all_outs_50_pa = sum(PA >= 50 & Out == 1)) %>%
               left_join(probs_check %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(
                 matched_to_table2 = n(), max_rate_diff_150_pa = max(rate_diff[PA_clean >= 150]),
                 median_abs_PA_diff = median(abs(PA - PA_clean)), max_abs_PA_diff = max(abs(PA - PA_clean))), by = "season") %>%
               left_join(table2 %>% count(season, name = "table2_rows"), by = "season"),
             digits = 3, caption = "Supplied probabilities workbook against Table 2")
write.csv(stats_check %>% select(Team, Season, Player, PA, OBP, SLG, OPS, status, duplicate_name),
          "quality/supplied_stats_check.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
```

```{r supplied-summary, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
cat("\n")
if (have_supplied) {
  mislabeled <- stats_check %>% filter(status == "previous season's line")
  dup_names <- stats_check %>% filter(duplicate_name) %>% distinct(Team, Season, key)
  short <- supplied_stats %>% count(Team, Season) %>% filter(n < 9)
  probs_2026 <- supplied_probs %>% filter(season == 2026)
  probs_ok <- probs_check %>% filter(season < 2026, PA_clean >= 150)
  cat(sprintf(paste("- **Statistics workbook.** %d rows labeled %s are the previous season's official lines, and %d names",
                    "appear twice with different numbers. A name-based de-duplication keeps an arbitrary copy, so a lineup",
                    "built from this file can mix seasons. %s, too few for a lineup of nine.\n"),
              nrow(mislabeled), paste(unique(paste(mislabeled$Team, mislabeled$Season)), collapse = ", "), nrow(dup_names),
              paste(paste(short$Team, short$Season, "has", short$n, ifelse(short$n == 1, "hitter", "hitters")), collapse = "; ")))
  cat(sprintf(paste("- **Probabilities workbook.** All %d of its 2026 rows have `Out` = 1 and every other outcome 0, so 2026",
                    "cannot be simulated from it. For 2023-2025 regulars (150+ PA) it agrees with Table 2 to within %.3f",
                    "in every outcome rate.\n"),
              nrow(probs_2026), max(probs_ok$rate_diff)))
} else {
  cat("- The supplied workbooks are not in this folder, so this comparison is skipped.\n")
}
cat("- Tables 1 and 2 above replace both workbooks for everything that follows.\n")
```

# Hitters and Batting Orders

## Player Characteristics from the Previous Season

The batting order for season *Y* is set from each hitter's MLB totals (all teams combined) in season *Y* − 1, with at least 100 PA. A hitter with fewer than 100 PA in *Y* − 1, for example after an injury, uses *Y* − 2 and *Y* − 1 pooled, again with at least 100 PA. A hitter with neither has no prior record (usually a rookie) and is not used.

```{r characteristics}
pooled <- function(ss) league %>% filter(season %in% ss) %>% group_by(batter_id) %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(count_cols), sum), .groups = "drop") %>% add_rates()
characteristics <- function(y) {
  prev <- pooled(y - 1) %>% filter(pa >= 100) %>% mutate(char_source = "previous season")
  two <- pooled(c(y - 2, y - 1)) %>% filter(pa >= 100, !batter_id %in% prev$batter_id) %>%
    mutate(char_source = "previous two seasons")
  bind_rows(prev, two) %>% mutate(season = y, char_pa = pa)
}
chars_main <- bind_rows(lapply(seasons, characteristics))
```

## Nine Hitters per Team-Season

Scope section 3: nine hitters chosen by plate appearances, preferring at least 150 PA. Here, the nine hitters with the most official PA for the team in that season, among those with a prior record. Ties go to the lower player ID, so the selection is reproducible.

```{r select-hitters}
candidates <- player_stats %>% select(season, team, batter_id, player, team_pa = pa) %>%
  left_join(chars_main %>% select(season, batter_id, char_source, char_pa), by = c("season", "batter_id")) %>%
  group_by(season, team) %>% arrange(desc(team_pa), batter_id, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(has_prior = !is.na(char_source), selected = has_prior & cumsum(has_prior) <= 9) %>% ungroup()
selected <- candidates %>% filter(selected)
stopifnot(all(count(selected, season, team)$n == 9))

knitr::kable(candidates %>% group_by(season, team) %>%
               summarise(hitters_150_pa = sum(team_pa >= 150), lowest_selected_pa = min(team_pa[selected]),
                         using_two_seasons = sum(selected & char_source == "previous two seasons"), .groups = "drop") %>%
               arrange(season, match(team, names(team_ids))),
             caption = "Selection by team-season")
skipped <- candidates %>% group_by(season, team) %>% filter(!has_prior, team_pa > min(team_pa[selected])) %>% ungroup()
knitr::kable(skipped %>% select(season, team, player, team_pa), caption = "Regulars skipped for lack of a prior record")
```

- Every selected hitter has at least `r min(selected$team_pa)` team PA, so all 180 meet the scope's 150-PA preference.
- `r nrow(skipped)` regulars across the 20 team-seasons are skipped, nearly all rookies. This is the price of setting the order from information available before the season; the next hitter by PA takes their place.

## Batting Orders A and B

Page-2 rules applied to each team-season's nine:

- **Traditional (A):** slot 1 highest OBP; slot 2 next-highest OBP; slot 3 highest remaining OPS; slot 4 highest remaining SLG; slot 5 highest remaining OPS; slots 6-9 by OPS, high to low.
- **OPS-ranked (B):** A's top five re-sorted by OPS; slots 6-9 same as A.

Ties go to the hitter with more team PA.

```{r lineup-rules}
make_hitters <- function(chars, picks = selected) {
  picks %>% select(season, team, batter_id, player, team_pa) %>% arrange(season, team, desc(team_pa), batter_id) %>%
    left_join(chars %>% select(season, batter_id, obp, slg, ops), by = c("season", "batter_id"))
}
slot_metric <- c("obp", "obp", "ops", "slg", "ops", "ops", "ops", "ops", "ops")
traditional_order <- function(d) {  # row numbers of d in batting order
  remaining <- seq_len(nrow(d))
  out <- integer(0)
  for (j in 1:9) {
    best <- remaining[which.max(d[[slot_metric[j]]][remaining])]
    out <- c(out, best)
    remaining <- setdiff(remaining, best)
  }
  out
}
ops_order <- function(d) {
  a <- traditional_order(d)
  c(a[1:5][order(-d$ops[a[1:5]])], a[6:9])  # order() is stable, so ties keep A's order
}
ops_all_order <- function(d) order(-d$ops)  # page-3 reading of B: all nine by OPS

hitters <- make_hitters(chars_main)
stopifnot(!anyNA(hitters$ops))
team_seasons <- expand.grid(team = names(team_ids), season = seasons, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[c("season", "team")]
get_nine <- function(h, i) filter(h, season == team_seasons$season[i], team == team_seasons$team[i])

order_table <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(team_seasons)), function(i) {
  d <- get_nine(hitters, i); a <- traditional_order(d); b <- ops_order(d)
  rbind(data.frame(team_seasons[i, ], order = "A", t(d$player[a])),
        data.frame(team_seasons[i, ], order = "B", t(d$player[b])))
}))
names(order_table)[4:12] <- paste0("slot", 1:9)
knitr::kable(order_table %>% select(season:slot5) %>%
               group_by(season, team) %>% mutate(same = if (n_distinct(paste(slot1, slot2, slot3, slot4, slot5)) == 1) "same" else "") %>%
               ungroup(), caption = "Slots 1-5 of orders A and B (slots 6-9 are identical)", row.names = FALSE)
```

- A and B differ only inside the top five. When A's top five already happen to be in OPS order, the two rules give the same lineup and B minus A is exactly zero.

# Simulation Model

## Base-Out Transitions by Season

For every plate appearance used, the base-out state before the play, the outcome, the state after, and the runs scored, estimated separately for each season. One textbook-advancement pseudo-observation per cell keeps rare cells sensible.

```{r transitions}
# State index 1-24: outs * 8 + bases + 1, with bases a bitmask (1 = first, 2 = second, 4 = third); 25 = three outs.
# Outcome of a transition: (next state, runs 0-4), stored as column (next - 1) * 5 + runs + 1.
pa_rows <- used %>% filter(is_pa, balanced) %>%
  mutate(from = pre_outs * 8L + pre_bases + 1L, to = ifelse(outs >= 3, 25L, outs * 8L + bases + 1L),
         combo = (to - 1L) * 5L + pmin(runs, 4) + 1L)
nK <- length(categories)
next_state <- rep(1:25, each = 5); combo_runs <- rep(0:4, times = 25)

# Deterministic advancement on outcome k from state s, returned as a combo column.
# ROE is treated like a single; outs never move runners.
move <- function(s, k, second_scores_on_single = FALSE) {
  o <- (s - 1) %/% 8; b <- (s - 1) %% 8
  r1 <- b %% 2 == 1; r2 <- b %/% 2 %% 2 == 1; r3 <- b %/% 4 == 1
  runs <- 0
  if (k %in% c("K", "OUT")) o <- o + 1
  if (k == "HR") { runs <- r1 + r2 + r3 + 1; b <- 0 }
  if (k == "3B") { runs <- r1 + r2 + r3; b <- 4 }
  if (k == "2B") { runs <- r2 + r3; b <- 2 + 4 * r1 }
  if (k %in% c("1B", "ROE")) {
    if (second_scores_on_single) { runs <- r2 + r3; b <- 1 + 2 * r1 } else { runs <- r3; b <- 1 + 2 * r1 + 4 * r2 }
  }
  if (k == "BB") { runs <- r1 & r2 & r3; b <- 1 + 2 * (r1 | r2) + 4 * (r3 | (r1 & r2)) }
  if (o >= 3) 24 * 5 + 1 else (o * 8 + b) * 5 + runs + 1
}
textbook_move <- function(s, k) move(s, k)
# The PM's notebook: runner on second scores on a single, errors are forced advances like walks.
notebook_move <- function(s, k) if (k == "ROE") move(s, "BB") else move(s, k, second_scores_on_single = TRUE)

build_model <- function(rows, mv) {
  n <- array(0, c(nK, 24, 125), dimnames = list(categories, NULL, NULL))
  if (!is.null(rows)) {
    tab <- rows %>% count(category, from, combo)
    n[cbind(match(tab$category, categories), tab$from, tab$combo)] <- tab$n
  }
  p <- n
  for (k in seq_len(nK)) for (s in 1:24) {
    c0 <- mv(s, categories[k])
    p[k, s, c0] <- p[k, s, c0] + 1
    p[k, s, ] <- p[k, s, ] / sum(p[k, s, ])
  }
  list(n = n, p = p,
       M = lapply(seq_len(nK), function(k) t(rowsum(t(p[k, , ]), next_state))),  # 24 x 25
       ER = lapply(seq_len(nK), function(k) drop(p[k, , ] %*% combo_runs)),     # expected runs, 24
       flat = do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nK), function(k) p[k, , ])))         # row (k - 1) * 24 + state
}
models <- setNames(lapply(seasons, function(y) build_model(filter(pa_rows, season == y), textbook_move)), seasons)
notebook_model <- build_model(NULL, notebook_move)
sapply(models, function(m) { cn <- apply(m$n, c(1, 2), sum); c(cells = length(cn), cells_under_20 = sum(cn < 20), smallest = min(cn)) })
```

```{r advancement-rates}
# Familiar advancement rates by season, as a sanity check of the transition tables.
rate <- function(k, from_bases, out_set, ok) sapply(seasons, function(y) {
  d <- filter(pa_rows, season == y, category == k, pre_bases == from_bases, pre_outs %in% out_set)
  round(mean(ok(d)), 3)
})
adv <- rbind(
  "Runner on 2nd scores on a single (<2 outs)" = rate("1B", 2, 0:1, function(d) d$runs >= 1),
  "Runner on 1st reaches 3rd or scores on a single (<2 outs)" = rate("1B", 1, 0:1, function(d) d$bases >= 4 | d$runs >= 1),
  "Runner on 1st scores on a double" = rate("2B", 1, 0:2, function(d) d$runs >= 1),
  "Double play on an out in play, runner on 1st (0 outs)" = rate("OUT", 1, 0, function(d) d$outs - d$pre_outs >= 2),
  "Runner on 3rd scores on an out in play (0-1 outs)" = rate("OUT", 4, 0:1, function(d) d$runs >= 1))
colnames(adv) <- seasons
knitr::kable(adv)
```

The PM's notebook uses fixed rules instead: a runner on second always scores on a single, a runner on first stops at second, and outs never move runners or turn double plays. The table shows how far real baserunning is from those rules; the stability section runs the results under them too.

## Exact Expected Runs (Markov Chain)

Each hitter's outcome rates mix the eight transition matrices into one 24-state chain. The half-inning starts with nobody on and nobody out and ends at three outs. The next inning starts with the hitter after the one who made the last out, so the lineup carries over between innings. Expected runs over nine innings follow exactly from the chain, with no simulation noise.

```{r markov}
batter_step <- function(p, model) list(T = Reduce(`+`, Map(`*`, p, model$M)), R = Reduce(`+`, Map(`*`, p, model$ER)))

# Expected runs in a half-inning led off by slot `lead`, and where the next inning starts.
inning_runs <- function(steps, lead) {
  v <- c(1, numeric(23)); b <- lead; runs <- 0; nxt <- numeric(9)
  while (sum(v) > 1e-12) {
    runs <- runs + sum(v * steps[[b]]$R)
    w <- drop(v %*% steps[[b]]$T)
    b <- b %% 9 + 1
    nxt[b] <- nxt[b] + w[25]
    v <- w[1:24]
  }
  c(runs, nxt)
}

# Expected runs in nine innings for a 9 x 8 matrix of outcome rates in batting order.
expected_runs <- function(p_mat, model) {
  steps <- lapply(1:9, function(i) batter_step(p_mat[i, ], model))
  inn <- sapply(1:9, function(j) inning_runs(steps, j))
  lead <- c(1, numeric(8)); total <- 0
  for (t in 1:9) {
    total <- total + sum(lead * inn[1, ])
    lead <- drop(lead %*% t(inn[-1, ]))
  }
  total
}
```

## Model Checks (Predictability)

**Run expectancy.** Average runs from each base-out state to the end of the inning, for a hitter with the season's average outcome rates, against the observed average. The observed values also include runs from steals, wild pitches, and pickoffs between plate appearances, which the model leaves out.

```{r re24}
bases_label <- c("---", "1--", "-2-", "12-", "--3", "1-3", "-23", "123")
re_by_season <- lapply(seasons, function(y) {
  rows <- filter(pa_rows, season == y)
  avg_p <- as.numeric(table(factor(rows$category, levels = categories)) / nrow(rows))
  st <- batter_step(avg_p, models[[as.character(y)]])
  re_model <- solve(diag(24) - st$T[, 1:24], st$R)
  obs <- used %>% filter(season == y, is_pa, inning <= 8) %>% group_by(state = pre_outs * 8 + pre_bases + 1) %>%
    summarise(observed = mean(runs_rest))
  list(re = re_model, avg_p = avg_p, freq = tabulate(rows$from, 24) / nrow(rows),
       table = data.frame(season = y, state = 1:24, model = re_model) %>% left_join(obs, by = "state"))
})
names(re_by_season) <- seasons
re_all <- bind_rows(lapply(re_by_season, `[[`, "table"))
knitr::kable(re_all %>% group_by(season) %>%
               summarise(start_model = model[state == 1], start_observed = observed[state == 1],
                         mean_abs_diff = mean(abs(model - observed)), max_abs_diff = max(abs(model - observed))),
             digits = 3, caption = "Run expectancy: model vs observed")
knitr::kable(re_all %>% filter(season == max(seasons)) %>%
               mutate(outs = (state - 1) %/% 8, bases = bases_label[(state - 1) %% 8 + 1]) %>%
               select(bases, outs, model, observed) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = outs, values_from = c(model, observed)) %>%
               select(bases, model_0, observed_0, model_1, observed_1, model_2, observed_2),
             digits = 3, caption = paste("Run expectancy by state,", max(seasons)))
```

**Team scoring.** Runs per inning (innings 1-8) for each team-season's offense, against the model fed nine copies of the team's overall outcome rates for that season.

```{r team-calibration}
team_obs <- plays %>% filter(inning <= 8, !is.na(team)) %>% group_by(season, team) %>%
  summarise(observed = sum(runs) / n_distinct(paste(game_id, inning)), .groups = "drop")
team_rates <- pbp_counts %>% group_by(season, team) %>% summarise(across(all_of(categories), sum), .groups = "drop")
calibration <- team_rates %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(team_average_hitters = expected_runs(matrix(c_across(all_of(categories)) / sum(c_across(all_of(categories))),
                                                     9, nK, byrow = TRUE), models[[as.character(season)]]) / 9) %>%
  ungroup() %>% select(season, team, team_average_hitters) %>% left_join(team_obs, by = c("season", "team"))
```

# Results

## Expected Runs Under A and B

```{r results}
rates_for <- function(d) {
  i <- match(paste(d$season, d$team, d$batter_id), paste(pbp_counts$season, pbp_counts$team, pbp_counts$batter_id))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(i))
  n <- as.matrix(pbp_counts[i, categories])
  list(counts = n, p = n / rowSums(n))
}
run_team <- function(d, model, b_rule = ops_order) {
  r <- rates_for(d)
  a <- traditional_order(d); b <- b_rule(d)
  list(season = d$season[1], team = d$team[1], counts = r$counts, p = r$p, a = a, b = b, model = model,
       runs_a = expected_runs(r$p[a, ], model), runs_b = expected_runs(r$p[b, ], model))
}
main <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(team_seasons)), function(i)
  run_team(get_nine(hitters, i), models[[as.character(team_seasons$season[i])]]))
results <- bind_rows(lapply(main, function(r) data.frame(
  season = r$season, team = r$team, slots_moved = sum(r$a != r$b), runs_per_game_A = r$runs_a,
  runs_per_game_B = r$runs_b, B_minus_A = r$runs_b - r$runs_a, B_minus_A_per_162 = 162 * (r$runs_b - r$runs_a))))

calibration <- calibration %>% left_join(results %>% transmute(season, team, selected_nine_A = runs_per_game_A / 9),
                                         by = c("season", "team"))
knitr::kable(calibration %>% select(season, team, observed, team_average_hitters, selected_nine_A) %>%
               arrange(season, match(team, names(team_ids))), digits = 3,
             caption = "Runs per inning: observed vs model")
```

```{r calibration-numbers, include=FALSE}
cal_diff <- calibration$observed - calibration$team_average_hitters
weaker_nine <- calibration %>% filter(selected_nine_A < team_average_hitters)
```

- With team-average hitters the model is within `r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(cal_diff)))` runs per inning of the observed rate in every team-season; observed minus model averages `r sprintf("%+.3f", mean(cal_diff))`. The model leaves out steals and other baserunning between plate appearances and gives every team the same baserunning, and real teams also score more or fewer runs than their hits and walks imply, depending on how they cluster. A and B share these gaps.
- The selected nine usually score more than the team average because bench players are left out. The exceptions (`r paste(weaker_nine$team, weaker_nine$season, collapse = ", ")`) are team-seasons where productive rookies without a prior record were skipped.

## Uncertainty from Player Rates

Each hitter's rates are estimates from a few hundred plate appearances. A parametric bootstrap redraws each hitter's outcome counts from a multinomial with his observed rates and recomputes B minus A. The batting orders stay fixed, because they were set from the previous season.

```{r bootstrap}
set.seed(534)
n_boot <- 1000
boot <- bind_rows(lapply(main, function(r) {
  if (all(r$a == r$b)) return(data.frame(season = r$season, team = r$team, ci_low = 0, ci_high = 0, share_B_better = 0))
  pa <- rowSums(r$counts)
  diffs <- replicate(n_boot, {
    p_star <- t(sapply(seq_along(pa), function(i) rmultinom(1, pa[i], r$p[i, ]) / pa[i]))
    expected_runs(p_star[r$b, ], r$model) - expected_runs(p_star[r$a, ], r$model)
  })
  data.frame(season = r$season, team = r$team, ci_low = unname(quantile(diffs, 0.025)),
             ci_high = unname(quantile(diffs, 0.975)), share_B_better = mean(diffs > 0))
}))
results <- results %>% left_join(boot, by = c("season", "team"))
knitr::kable(results, digits = 4, caption = "Expected runs per nine innings; B minus A with 95% bootstrap interval")
write.csv(results, "processed/simulation_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r results-plot, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=6}
par(mar = c(4, 9, 2, 1))
y <- rev(seq_len(nrow(results)))
plot(results$B_minus_A, y, xlim = range(c(results$ci_low, results$ci_high, 0)), yaxt = "n", pch = 19,
     col = "#2a78d6", xlab = "B minus A, runs per nine innings", ylab = "", main = "OPS-ranked (B) minus Traditional (A)")
segments(results$ci_low, y, results$ci_high, y, col = "#2a78d6", lwd = 2)
abline(v = 0, col = "#9a9a9a", lty = 2)
abline(h = y[results$team == "Giants"][-length(seasons)] - 0.5, col = "#dddddd")
axis(2, at = y, labels = paste(results$team, results$season), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.85)
```

## Across Team-Seasons: the Scope's t-Test

The scope plans a t-test of runs under the two orders. Within one team-season a t-test on simulated games only measures simulation noise (see the Monte Carlo check). The meaningful version treats each team-season as one paired observation: its exact B minus A.

```{r t-test}
moved <- results %>% filter(slots_moved > 0)
tt_all <- t.test(results$B_minus_A)
tt_moved <- t.test(moved$B_minus_A)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  sample = c("All 20 team-seasons", "Team-seasons where A and B differ"),
  n = c(nrow(results), nrow(moved)), mean_B_minus_A = c(tt_all$estimate, tt_moved$estimate),
  ci_low = c(tt_all$conf.int[1], tt_moved$conf.int[1]), ci_high = c(tt_all$conf.int[2], tt_moved$conf.int[2]),
  p_value = c(tt_all$p.value, tt_moved$p.value), B_better = c(sum(results$B_minus_A > 0), sum(moved$B_minus_A > 0))),
  digits = 4, caption = "One-sample t-test of B minus A (runs per nine innings) across team-seasons")
```

## Monte Carlo Check

The same model, simulated game by game: 50,000 nine-inning games per order and team-season. This checks the exact calculation and shows the spread of runs.

```{r monte-carlo}
simulate_games <- function(p_mat, n_games, model) {
  cum_p <- t(apply(p_mat, 1, cumsum)); cum_p[, nK] <- 1
  runs <- matrix(0L, n_games, 9)
  lead <- rep(1L, n_games)
  for (inn in 1:9) {
    s <- rep(1L, n_games); b <- lead; active <- seq_len(n_games)
    while (length(active) > 0) {
      k <- 1L + rowSums(runif(length(active)) > cum_p[b[active], , drop = FALSE])
      row <- (k - 1L) * 24L + s[active]
      combo <- integer(length(active))
      groups <- split(seq_along(row), row)
      for (g in names(groups)) {
        j <- groups[[g]]
        combo[j] <- sample.int(125L, length(j), replace = TRUE, prob = model$flat[as.integer(g), ])
      }
      runs[active, inn] <- runs[active, inn] + (combo - 1L) %% 5L
      b[active] <- b[active] %% 9L + 1L
      s[active] <- (combo - 1L) %/% 5L + 1L
      active <- active[s[active] != 25L]
    }
    lead <- b
  }
  runs
}

set.seed(2026)
n_games <- 50000
mc <- bind_rows(lapply(main, function(r) {
  ga <- rowSums(simulate_games(r$p[r$a, ], n_games, r$model))
  gb <- if (all(r$a == r$b)) ga else rowSums(simulate_games(r$p[r$b, ], n_games, r$model))
  data.frame(season = r$season, team = r$team, exact_A = r$runs_a, mc_A = mean(ga), exact_B = r$runs_b, mc_B = mean(gb),
             mc_se = sd(ga) / sqrt(n_games), sd_runs_per_game = sd(ga), shutout_A = mean(ga == 0))
}))
knitr::kable(mc, digits = 3, caption = "Exact vs Monte Carlo runs per nine innings")
stopifnot(all(abs(mc$mc_A - mc$exact_A) < 4 * mc$mc_se), all(abs(mc$mc_B - mc$exact_B) < 4 * mc$mc_se))
```

- Every Monte Carlo mean is within `r sprintf("%.1f", max(abs(c(mc$mc_A - mc$exact_A, mc$mc_B - mc$exact_B)) / mc$mc_se))` standard errors of the exact value.
- Runs in one game have a standard deviation of about `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(mc$sd_runs_per_game))`. With *n* simulated games, the standard error of a difference of two means is about `r sprintf("%.1f", mean(mc$sd_runs_per_game))` × √(2/*n*): 0.03 runs at 20,000 games. Differences of a few hundredths of a run need the exact calculation or millions of games.

## How Much Can Order Matter?

To show the model does respond to batting order, the same nine hitters sorted by OPS from high to low and from low to high. `gap_prev_ops` sorts by previous-season OPS, the information A and B use; `gap_same_ops` sorts by that season's OPS, which is hindsight.

```{r order-scale}
chars_same <- league %>% filter(season %in% seasons) %>% add_rates()
order_scale <- bind_rows(lapply(main, function(r) {
  d <- filter(hitters, season == r$season, team == r$team)
  ops_same <- chars_same$ops[match(paste(d$season, d$batter_id), paste(chars_same$season, chars_same$batter_id))]
  best_prev <- order(-d$ops); best_same <- order(-ops_same)
  data.frame(season = r$season, team = r$team,
             gap_prev_ops = expected_runs(r$p[best_prev, ], r$model) - expected_runs(r$p[rev(best_prev), ], r$model),
             gap_same_ops = expected_runs(r$p[best_same, ], r$model) - expected_runs(r$p[rev(best_same), ], r$model))
})) %>% mutate(gap_same_per_162 = 162 * gap_same_ops)
knitr::kable(order_scale, digits = 3, caption = "Runs per nine innings, best-first minus worst-first")
```

- With hindsight, reversing the order costs `r sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(order_scale$gap_same_ops), max(order_scale$gap_same_ops))` runs per game, about `r round(min(order_scale$gap_same_per_162))`-`r round(max(order_scale$gap_same_per_162))` runs over a season, so the model does detect order effects.
- Sorted by previous-season OPS, the gap ranges from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(order_scale$gap_prev_ops))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(order_scale$gap_prev_ops))` runs per game, and in `r sum(order_scale$gap_prev_ops < 0)` team-seasons the reversed order even scores more. How well last season predicts this one limits what any order rule can gain.

## Why A and B Are So Close

Moving a hitter changes runs mainly by changing how often he bats. Each hitter is valued in runs above an average plate appearance, using run values for each outcome from the model's run expectancy.

```{r why-close}
# Expected plate appearances per batting slot in a nine-inning game.
pa_by_slot <- function(p_mat, model) {
  steps <- lapply(1:9, function(i) batter_step(p_mat[i, ], model))
  inn <- lapply(1:9, function(j) {
    v <- c(1, numeric(23)); b <- j; pa <- numeric(9); nxt <- numeric(9)
    while (sum(v) > 1e-12) {
      pa[b] <- pa[b] + sum(v)
      w <- drop(v %*% steps[[b]]$T)
      b <- b %% 9 + 1
      nxt[b] <- nxt[b] + w[25]
      v <- w[1:24]
    }
    list(pa = pa, nxt = nxt)
  })
  L <- t(sapply(inn, `[[`, "nxt")); P <- t(sapply(inn, `[[`, "pa"))
  lead <- c(1, numeric(8)); total <- numeric(9)
  for (t in 1:9) { total <- total + drop(lead %*% P); lead <- drop(lead %*% L) }
  total
}

# Run value of each outcome: change in run expectancy plus runs scored, averaged over the states where PAs happen.
run_values <- t(sapply(seasons, function(y) {
  m <- models[[as.character(y)]]; re <- re_by_season[[as.character(y)]]
  setNames(sapply(seq_len(nK), function(k) sum(re$freq * (drop(m$M[[k]] %*% c(re$re, 0)) + m$ER[[k]] - re$re))), categories)
}))
rownames(run_values) <- seasons
knitr::kable(run_values, digits = 3, caption = "Run value of each outcome, relative to an average plate appearance")

slot_pa <- t(sapply(main, function(r) pa_by_slot(r$p[r$a, ], r$model)))
knitr::kable(t(colMeans(slot_pa)) %>% `colnames<-`(paste("slot", 1:9)), digits = 2,
             caption = "Plate appearances per game by slot (order A, average over team-seasons)")

pa_effect <- bind_rows(lapply(main, function(r) {
  slot_a <- match(seq_len(9), r$a); slot_b <- match(seq_len(9), r$b)
  mv <- which(slot_a != slot_b)
  if (length(mv) == 0) return(NULL)
  pa_a <- pa_by_slot(r$p[r$a, ], r$model)
  value <- drop(r$p %*% run_values[as.character(r$season), ])
  data.frame(season = r$season, team = r$team, PA_effect = sum(value[mv] * (pa_a[slot_b[mv]] - pa_a[slot_a[mv]])))
})) %>% left_join(results %>% select(season, team, exact_B_minus_A = B_minus_A), by = c("season", "team")) %>%
  mutate(sequencing_effect = exact_B_minus_A - PA_effect)
knitr::kable(pa_effect, digits = 4, caption = "B minus A split into plate appearances and sequencing (runs per game)")
```

- Each slot down the order bats about `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(-diff(colMeans(slot_pa))))` fewer times per game, about `r round(162 * mean(-diff(colMeans(slot_pa))))` plate appearances over a season. Swapping two hitters who are 0.05 runs per PA apart changes about 0.11 × 0.05 ≈ 0.005 runs per game.
- The rest is sequencing: who bats ahead of whom, for example a high-OBP hitter in front of a power hitter. It is of the same small size and often has the opposite sign.
- The scope's Traditional rule already bats the highest-OBP hitter first, which is close to what analysts recommend. It is not the old-style lineup with a fast, low-OBP leadoff hitter and the best hitter third, so B has little left to improve.

## Stability Checks

Each row changes one judgment call and recomputes B minus A for all 20 team-seasons with the same nine hitters.

```{r sensitivity}
chars_two <- bind_rows(lapply(seasons, function(y) pooled(c(y - 2, y - 1)) %>% mutate(season = y)))
scenario <- function(name, chars, b_rule = ops_order, notebook = FALSE) {
  h <- make_hitters(chars)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(h$ops))
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(team_seasons)), function(i) {
    m <- if (notebook) notebook_model else models[[as.character(team_seasons$season[i])]]
    r <- run_team(get_nine(h, i), m, b_rule)
    data.frame(scenario = name, season = r$season, team = r$team, slots_moved = sum(r$a != r$b),
               runs_A = r$runs_a, B_minus_A = r$runs_b - r$runs_a)
  }))
}
sensitivity <- bind_rows(
  scenario("Main: previous-season characteristics", chars_main),
  scenario("Same-season characteristics (hindsight, as in the PM's notebook)", chars_same),
  scenario("Two prior seasons pooled", chars_two),
  scenario("B = all nine by OPS (page-3 table)", chars_main, ops_all_order),
  scenario("Fixed base-running rules from the PM's notebook", chars_main, notebook = TRUE))
write.csv(sensitivity, "processed/simulation_sensitivity.csv", row.names = FALSE)
sens_summary <- sensitivity %>% group_by(scenario = factor(scenario, unique(scenario))) %>%
  summarise(orders_differ = sum(slots_moved > 0), mean_runs_A = mean(runs_A), mean_B_minus_A = mean(B_minus_A),
            min = min(B_minus_A), max = max(B_minus_A), B_better = sum(B_minus_A > 0), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(sens_summary, digits = 4, caption = "B minus A (runs per nine innings) across 20 team-seasons, by scenario")
```

- The largest B minus A in absolute value in any scenario is `r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(sensitivity$B_minus_A)))` runs per game, about `r sprintf("%.1f", 162 * max(abs(sensitivity$B_minus_A)))` runs over a season.

```{r save-outputs}
lineup_out <- bind_rows(lapply(main, function(r) {
  d <- filter(hitters, season == r$season, team == r$team) %>%
    left_join(candidates %>% select(season, batter_id, team, char_source, char_pa), by = c("season", "team", "batter_id"))
  data.frame(d, r$p, slot_A = match(seq_len(9), r$a), slot_B = match(seq_len(9), r$b), check.names = FALSE)
}))
write.csv(lineup_out, "processed/simulation_lineups.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
write.csv(pa_rows %>% count(season, category, from, combo) %>%
            mutate(next_state = (combo - 1) %/% 5 + 1, runs = (combo - 1) %% 5) %>% select(-combo),
          "processed/simulation_transitions.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Conclusion

```{r conclusion-numbers, include=FALSE}
n_same <- sum(results$slots_moved == 0)
excludes_zero <- moved %>% filter(ci_low > 0 | ci_high < 0)
```

- With the same nine hitters, the OPS-ranked order (B) and the Traditional order (A) produce practically the same expected runs in all 20 team-seasons.
  - In `r n_same` team-seasons the two rules give the identical lineup.
  - Where they differ, B minus A is `r sprintf("%.4f", min(moved$B_minus_A))` to `r sprintf("%.4f", max(moved$B_minus_A))` runs per game, or `r sprintf("%.1f", min(moved$B_minus_A_per_162))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(moved$B_minus_A_per_162))` runs over 162 games.
  - `r nrow(excludes_zero)` of `r nrow(moved)` bootstrap intervals exclude zero (`r paste(excludes_zero$team, excludes_zero$season, collapse = ", ")`), about what chance alone gives with `r nrow(moved)` intervals at the 95% level (`r sprintf("%.1f", 0.05 * nrow(moved))` expected).
  - Across team-seasons the mean B minus A is `r sprintf("%.4f", tt_all$estimate)` runs per game (95% CI `r sprintf("%.4f to %.4f", tt_all$conf.int[1], tt_all$conf.int[2])`, *p* = `r sprintf("%.2f", tt_all$p.value)`).
- No stability check changes this: the largest absolute difference in any scenario is `r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(sensitivity$B_minus_A)))` runs per game, including the PM's same-season characteristics and fixed base-running rules.
- The model does respond to order: with hindsight, reversing a lineup costs `r sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(order_scale$gap_same_ops), max(order_scale$gap_same_ops))` runs per game. Rearranging two to five hitters within the top five is too small a change to matter.
- The answer to the research question: neither order produces meaningfully more runs. Who is in the lineup matters far more than which of these two orders is used.

**Limitations.** Baserunning is the same for every hitter and team within a season. Steals, pickoffs, and wild pitches between plate appearances are left out. Opposing pitchers are not modeled. Nine full innings are played every game. These affect A and B in the same way, so they matter much less for the difference than for the run totals.
